correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, inverse preimages of a and b give an interval-growth process. At least n−1 productive inverse b steps and n−1 inverse rotations between successive productive steps force length >=(n−1)^2. Equality gives the unique word W. With one extra letter, either one a is added at the leading boundary, yielding aW, or one b acts identically at a unique position in an existing a-run, yielding the explicit t!=j insertion family. All boundary cases, distinctness and the two already-reset trailing extensions are proved. Finite independent subset dynamic programming and explicit candidate simulation check every n=2..11 and return VERIFY_OK; the computations are not the proof.

value.rationale: The Černý automata are the canonical extremal family for synchronization. The first coefficient immediately beyond their sharp quadratic reset threshold quantitatively measures near-optimal synchronizing-word rigidity. An exact all-n count and complete insertion classification explain which modifications preserve first-time synchronization, a structural language problem not settled by a minimum-length value or a small finite table. It does not claim new bounds on the general Černý conjecture.
